lines.text: A state wildlife officer walks onto private land in West Tennessee, cuts a branch off a tree, and installs a camera on it.

He cuts a branch off it, and installs a camera on it.

shorts.angle: Tennessee wrote three constitutions and three times refused the federal word. Where the Fourth Amendment says effects, the state says possessions.
shorts.avoids: No claim the extra word decided the case on its own; no vote count for Welch; no assertion about any other state's constitution.

lines.text: The Fourth Amendment says a person is secure in their persons, houses, papers and effects.
source_lines: One word in that list is not in the federal one. The Fourth Amendment says effects.

lines.text: Tennessee wrote possessions.

lines.text: In 1834 it wrote a new one and kept possessions. In 1870 it wrote another and kept it again.

lines.text: It refers to property, real or personal, actually possessed or occupied.

shorts.angle: Three judges, no dissent, and an answer two sentences long: the statute is constitutional as written and unconstitutional as it was used.
shorts.avoids: No claim the statute was struck down; no injunction; no damages figure beyond nominal; no claim this binds another state.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: How can one law be lawful on its face and unlawful in the hands that used it?

lines.text: On May 9, 2024, the Tennessee Court of Appeals answered. Three judges, no dissent.

lines.text: We conclude the statute is facially constitutional but unconstitutional as applied.

lines.text: Two questions were in front of them, and they are not the same question.

lines.text: To lose on its face, a statute has to fail in every application it has.
source_lines: The statute has to fail in every application it has, and not merely in most of them.

lines.text: The plaintiffs had already conceded one. Entries onto wild waste land are constitutional.
source_lines: They do not dispute that the statute authorizes entries upon wild waste land areas or that such entries are constitutional under the Tennessee Constitution.

lines.text: One lawful use is enough to end a facial challenge. The state won that half.
source_lines: So there is at least one lawful use of the statute, and one is enough to end a facial challenge.
